topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, course structure, and learning objectives regarding cancer causes and environmental carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors and Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the fundamental origins of cancer by evaluating the interplay between intrinsic cellular errors, genetic predisposition, and environmental risk factors.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections drive cancer development, illustrated by the etiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how chemical carcinogens and radiation undergo metabolic activation and induce specific forms of DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic drivers of cancer development, including the initiator-promoter paradigm, chronic inflammation, and host developmental vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying Carcinogens and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine carcinogenicity and assess human cancer risk.
